subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: For provider-minted signed-thinking fields, should OpenClaw preserve structurally valid opaque replay tokens even when their bytes contain credential-shaped substrings, or keep the current redaction-idempotency gate and only harden individual secret patterns?
rationale: The current tests intentionally redact credential-shaped provider signature fields, but the report shows that policy can corrupt real opaque replay tokens; the durable fix changes the boundary between transcript secret redaction and provider-owned opaque bytes.

options.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
options.body: Preserve validated opaque signatures only in known provider signed-thinking fields while leaving arbitrary text, missing-route fields, and malformed payloads redacted.

options.title: Pattern-Only Hardening
options.body: Make fixed-case vendor prefixes and boundaries stricter while keeping the current redaction-idempotency requirement for provider signatures.

options.title: Send-Side Recovery Only
options.body: Drop visibly corrupted signatures on Bedrock/Anthropic send and rely on recovery without changing transcript-redaction preservation.

recommendation.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
recommendation.body: Preserve validated opaque signatures only in known provider signed-thinking fields while leaving arbitrary text, missing-route fields, and malformed payloads redacted.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the PR commits that scoped and validated the current provider replay signature boundary.
